say: Here's what I changed, starting next week: on Push and Upper I swapped in cable face pulls for more rear delt work and added a cable crunch finisher. On Pull and Lower I added cable rear delt flyes and hanging leg raises to hit rear delts and core twice a week. I kept your lateral raises, rows, and pulldowns since those are working, just traded out some of the redundant accessory lifts to make room. After Pull and Lower I tacked on an easy Peloton ride to get some low-impact cardio in without eating into recovery for squats and deadlifts.

I added cable face pulls on Pull and bumped up your rear delt work on Upper, so now rear delts get hit on Pull and Upper each week — that's your two to three times. On Pull I swapped the lateral raise for a face pull to make room, and on Upper I added a dumbbell rear delt fly in place of the barbell biceps curl since that session was light on rear delt work. Pull still keeps its rear delt fly too, so you're covered well.

I hear you - let's back the volume off. Starting next week I'm trimming the easy runs, the tempo run, and the long runs a bit each week, and giving you an extra rest day by taking day 3's easy run off the schedule entirely. Race week stays untouched so you go in fresh. We'll keep the taper and the race distance exactly as planned.

Let's keep your strength work but tip the scales toward fat loss. On Push, Pull, Upper and Lower I trimmed one of the slower accessory lifts and added a finisher of cable-rope-pushdown or curls stays, but swapped in a short conditioning burst plus an easy bike ride to each of those four sessions to raise your weekly calorie burn. I kept Legs as is since squats and deadlifts already do plenty of work there, and tightened nothing else about your rest days since the extra conditioning adds the burn without adding junk volume. Keep eating in a deficit — the training can only do part of this.
